newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, further losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, further losses seen.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the third session in a row hit by Friday Wall Street plunge and analysts said falls on world's stock exchanges and upcoming attractive primary offerings made a near-term rebound unlikely.

The main market's WIG index fell 417.2 points, or 2.6 percent, to 15,846.6, and turnover rose 7.5 percent to 160.9 million zlotys ($53.7 million) on all three markets as 80 issues fell, six rose and six were flat.
They said Warsaw was likely to fall or stay in horizontal trend with a slight falling tendency in the next few sessions, unless the climate on world's leading bourses improves.

"The market looks bad, we had falls in higher turnover despite strong Friday's buying...and investors increasingly watch foreign bourses before making any decisions," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria brokerage.

Analysts said Polish paper firm Celuloza Swiecie SA primary market offer of at least 112.5 million zlotys ($37.3 million), which starts on Tuesday and metals trader Impexmetal SA next week's offering worth at least 222 million zlotys ($74 million) could significantly draw capital from the bourse.
Some analysts said, however, a fall to 15,500 should spur some demand and help the bourse edge up.
They said Tuesday's inflation figure, expected relatively low at below one percent, was already priced-in but should contribute to the bourse's better performance in longer-term.
They said Polish central bank chief saying on Friday that the government should achieve its 13 percent inflation goal for 1997 also bode well in the longer-term.

Some said monthly earnings reports due later in the week could cause some sharp swings of selected stocks. They expected construction stocks to show strong earnings growth over last year, when they were hit by harsh winter.
